quotes.text: We’re trying to build a world where decision-makers are equipped to ensure powerful new technologies benefit all of humanity.
quotes.source: 2023 Impact Report Summary (BlueDot Impact)

quotes.text: Building AI safety and biosecurity talent infrastructure is tractable, neglected and desperately needed.
quotes.source: What we're building at BlueDot (blog)

name: Li-Lian Ang
photo_credit: Li-Lian Ang's homepage. Source: https://anglilian.com/
bio: Li-Lian Ang works at BlueDot Impact and writes guides for people starting out in AI safety. Her posts help learners decide which course fits them.
warning: Anyone who cares about the future and is ready to act can start learning AI safety.

quotes.text: We’ve designed these courses for driven individuals determined to make a real difference.
quotes.source: Am I the right fit for BlueDot's courses? (BlueDot blog)

quotes.text: Our courses are tailored for those who recognise the potential risks of emerging technologies and are motivated to take action to ensure they are used to benefit humanity positively.
quotes.source: Am I the right fit for BlueDot's courses? (BlueDot blog)

links.label: Am I the right fit for BlueDot's courses?

name: Sayash Kapoor
photo_credit: GWU Digital Trade and Data Governance Hub event page. Source: https://datagovhub.elliott.gwu.edu/calendar_event/ai-snake-oil-with-sayash-kapoor/
bio: Sayash Kapoor is a Princeton researcher who co-wrote AI Snake Oil and 'AI as Normal Technology' with Arvind Narayanan. He studies how AI claims hold up in the real world.
warning: We should treat AI as a powerful but normal technology and focus on how society adopts it.

quotes.text: AI as normal technology is a worldview that stands in contrast to the worldview of AI as impending superintelligence.
quotes.source: AI as Normal Technology (with Arvind Narayanan)

name: William Saunders
photo_credit: C-SPAN frame of his September 2024 US Senate Judiciary subcommittee testimony, via Lawrence Lessig on Medium. Source: https://lessig.medium.com/william-saunders-why-i-support-sb1047-5f93a462fa5e
bio: William Saunders worked on OpenAI's Superalignment team and resigned in 2024. He signed the 'A Right to Warn' letter and later spoke to the US Senate about safety at AI labs.
warning: Insiders must be free to warn the public when AI companies take serious risks.

quotes.text: These risks range from the further entrenchment of existing inequalities, to manipulation and misinformation, to the loss of control of autonomous AI systems potentially resulting in human extinction.
quotes.source: A Right to Warn about Advanced AI (open letter, signatory)

links.label: A Right to Warn about Advanced AI

left_lab.reason: He warned that weaker nonprofit control would give OpenAI more incentive to race and cut corners on safety.

name: Thomas Larsen
photo_credit: MATS mentor page. Source: https://www.matsprogram.org/mentor/larsen
agi_year: AI 2027 forecast a superhuman coder in early 2027 (April 2025 scenario)
bio: Thomas Larsen is a researcher at the AI Futures Project who works on AI policy and scenarios. He co-wrote the AI 2027 scenario.
warning: Superhuman AI this decade could change the world more than the Industrial Revolution.

quotes.text: We predict that the impact of superhuman AI over the next decade will be enormous, exceeding that of the Industrial Revolution.
quotes.source: AI 2027 scenario (co-author)

name: Lennart Heim
photo_credit: 80,000 Hours podcast guest page. Source: https://80000hours.org/podcast/episodes/lennart-heim-compute-governance/
bio: Lennart Heim researches compute governance, the idea of using control over AI chips and data centers as a lever for safety. He co-wrote Epoch AI's influential study of training compute trends.
warning: Compute is growing fast and is one of the few parts of AI that governments can measure and control.

quotes.text: Furthermore, we find that the training compute has grown by a factor of 10 billion since 2010, with a doubling rate of around 5-6 months.
quotes.source: Compute Trends Across Three Eras of Machine Learning (co-author, Epoch AI)

links.label: Compute Trends Across Three Eras of Machine Learning

name: John Schulman
bio: John Schulman is a co-founder of OpenAI and one of the main people behind reinforcement learning from human feedback. He is now chief scientist at Thinking Machines Lab.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier and says labs should build ways to slow down together, even before governments ask.

quotes.text: Signed because this statement helps establish common knowledge about the possible need for coordination mechanisms as automated AI research accelerates progress. I'd also like to see labs start designing these mechanisms voluntarily, even before the USG gets involved.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

background: He studied at Caltech and did his PhD at UC Berkeley. He then helped found OpenAI in 2015.

key_papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

name: Jakub Pachocki
photo_credit: ICPCNews, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jakub_Pachocki_in_2012_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Jakub Pachocki is a Polish computer scientist and the chief scientist of OpenAI. He led work on GPT-4.
warning: In September 2026 he wrote that no AI company has solved alignment well enough to keep scaling at full speed for much longer.

quotes.text: solved alignment and monitoring to a sufficient degree to continue responsibly scaling at maximum speed for much longer
quotes.source: Blog post, as quoted by CNBC

quotes.text: I expect and hope for voluntary slowdowns to become commonplace until shared safety bars are established
quotes.source: Blog post, as quoted by CNBC

background: He was a top competitive programmer, studied at the University of Warsaw and did his PhD at Carnegie Mellon University. He then did postdoctoral work at Harvard.

name: Jasjeet Sekhon
bio: Jasjeet Sekhon is a statistician and political scientist known for work on causal inference and machine learning. He is chief strategy officer at Google DeepMind.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier and says we must build tools to pace the riskiest capabilities before we need them.

quotes.text: We can capture the benefits of the coming intelligence explosion while managing its risks, but only if we build the tools to pace the frontier of the riskiest capabilities before we need them, so we protect people and keep the social trust that innovation depends on. I believe smart technical and governance tools will be needed to sustain rapid innovation, vigorous competition, and robust safety.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

background: He studied at Cornell University. He became the Eugene Meyer Professor at Yale University.

name: Wojciech Zaremba
bio: Wojciech Zaremba is a Polish computer scientist and a co-founder of OpenAI. He led its robotics work and later teams on GPT models, Codex and GitHub Copilot.
background: He studied at the University of Warsaw and Ecole Polytechnique, and did his PhD at New York University.

career.role: Lead, GPT, Codex and Copilot teams

key_papers.title: Intriguing properties of neural networks

name: Dawn Song
photo_credit: Xuthoria, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ICLR_2025_-_Dawn_Song_01.jpg)
bio: Dawn Song is a computer security expert and a professor at UC Berkeley. She won a MacArthur Fellowship in 2010.
warning: She signed Pacing the Frontier, warning that AI progress may move faster than society is ready for.

quotes.text: Frontier AI capabilities are advancing rapidly, and the pace of progress is itself accelerating. We see this directly in our evaluation work.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

background: She did her PhD at UC Berkeley and taught at Carnegie Mellon University before returning to Berkeley.

name: Boaz Barak
photo_credit: BöhmMartin, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Boaz_Barak_at_the_DIMACS_Workshop_on_Cryptography.jpg)
bio: Boaz Barak is a theoretical computer scientist and a professor at Harvard University. He also works on safety at OpenAI.
background: He studied at Tel Aviv University and did his PhD at the Weizmann Institute of Science. He taught at Princeton before Harvard.

name: Amanda Askell
bio: Amanda Askell is a Scottish philosopher who leads the team that shapes Claude's character and constitution at Anthropic. She was on the TIME 100 AI list in 2024.
background: She studied philosophy at Oxford and did her PhD at New York University. She worked at OpenAI before joining Anthropic in 2021.

key_papers.title: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment
Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

name: Nicholas Carlini
photo_credit: National Institute of Standards and Technology, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Nicholas_Carlini_AIME_presentation.jpg)
bio: Nicholas Carlini is a security researcher known for showing how machine learning systems can be fooled. His Carlini and Wagner attack broke many early defenses.
background: He did his PhD at UC Berkeley. He then worked at Google DeepMind before joining Anthropic.

key_papers.title: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Neural Networks
Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models

name: Dean W. Ball
bio: Dean Ball is an AI policy researcher. He was the main author of the 2025 US AI Action Plan at the White House.
background: He studied history at Hamilton College and worked at think tanks like the Mercatus Center and the Hoover Institution.

name: Timnit Gebru
photo_credit: TechCrunch, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Timnit_Gebru_crop.jpg)
bio: Timnit Gebru is a computer scientist who studies bias in AI. She co-founded Black in AI and founded the DAIR Institute.
warning: She warns that large language models carry real harms now, like bias and cost, and that big companies silence critics.

left_lab.reason: She left after a fight over a paper on the risks of large language models.

background: She did her PhD at Stanford University. She worked at Microsoft Research and then co-led the Ethical AI team at Google.

name: Margaret Mitchell
photo_credit: AI4LAM, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:MargaretMitchell2022.jpg)
bio: Margaret Mitchell studies bias and fairness in machine learning. She is known for model cards, a way to report what a model is for.

left_lab.reason: She was fired by Google a few months after Timnit Gebru left.

background: She studied at Reed College and did her PhD at the University of Aberdeen. She worked at Microsoft Research and co-led Ethical AI at Google.

key_papers.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting

name: Lawrence Lessig
photo_credit: lessig, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lessig_in_2024.png)
bio: Lawrence Lessig is a legal scholar at Harvard Law School and the founder of Creative Commons. He gave free legal help to AI workers who want to warn the public.
background: He studied at the University of Pennsylvania, Cambridge and Yale Law School. He taught at Chicago and Stanford before Harvard.

career.role: Roy L. Furman Professor of Law

name: David Krueger
bio: David Krueger is a machine learning professor who works to reduce risks from AI. He ran a safety lab at the University of Cambridge and is now at Mila.
warning: He started the 2023 Statement on AI Risk, which says AI could cause human extinction. He studies the risk of AI improving itself.
background: He did his PhD at the University of Montreal with Mila. He then taught at the University of Cambridge.

name: Brian Christian
photo_credit: Eileen Meny (Photographer), CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Brian_Christian_in_2019,_Photograph_by_Eileen_Meny_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Brian Christian is an author who writes about what computer science means for people. His book The Alignment Problem explains AI alignment in plain words.
background: He studied computer science and philosophy at Brown University, and poetry at the University of Washington.

name: Kai-Fu Lee
photo_credit: Press Service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kai-Fu_Lee_in_September_2026_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Kai-Fu Lee is a computer scientist and investor. He founded Microsoft Research Asia, ran Google China, and wrote AI Superpowers.
background: He studied at Columbia University and did his PhD at Carnegie Mellon University, where he built an early speech recognition system.

name: Kate Crawford
photo_credit: Cmichel67, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kate_Crawford_in_2025_05.jpg)
bio: Kate Crawford studies the social and political side of AI. She co-founded the AI Now Institute and wrote Atlas of AI in 2021.
background: She studied at the University of Sydney. She taught at the University of New South Wales before moving to New York.

name: Toby Walsh
photo_credit: Avobronte, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Toby_Walsh,_portrait.jpg)
bio: Toby Walsh is a professor of AI at UNSW Sydney and chief scientist of its AI institute. He helped lead open letters calling for a ban on autonomous weapons.
background: He studied at the University of Cambridge and did his PhD at the University of Edinburgh.

career.role: Laureate Fellow and Professor of AI

books.title: It's Alive!: Artificial Intelligence from the Logic Piano to Killer Robots
Machines Behaving Badly: the Morality of AI
Faking It: Artificial Intelligence in a Human World

name: Yuval Noah Harari
photo_credit: Martin Kraft, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:MKr364751_Yuval_Noah_Harari_(Frankfurter_Buchmesse_2024).jpg)
bio: Yuval Noah Harari is a historian and the author of Sapiens. His book Nexus looks at how AI could change who holds power over information.
background: He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and did his doctorate at Jesus College, Oxford.

name: Kaiming He
bio: Kaiming He is a computer vision researcher and one of the creators of ResNet. His 2016 ResNet paper is one of the most cited papers in all of science.
background: He studied at Tsinghua University and did his PhD at the Chinese University of Hong Kong in 2011.

key_papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
Mask R-CNN

name: Fei-Fei Li
photo_credit: ITU Pictures, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fei-Fei_Li_at_AI_for_Good_2017.jpg)
bio: Fei-Fei Li built ImageNet, the dataset that sped up computer vision in the 2010s. She co-directs the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI.
background: She studied physics at Princeton University and did her PhD at Caltech. She taught at the University of Illinois and Princeton before Stanford.

books.title: The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI

key_papers.title: ImageNet: A large-scale hierarchical image database
ImageNet large scale visual recognition challenge
Perceptual losses for real-time style transfer and super-resolution

name: Jurgen Schmidhuber
photo_credit: ITU/R.Farrell, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:J%C3%BCrgen_Schmidhuber,_2017_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Jurgen Schmidhuber is a German computer scientist best known for long short-term memory, or LSTM. He leads the Swiss AI lab IDSIA and the AI initiative at KAUST.
background: He was born in Munich and did his undergraduate degree and PhD at the Technical University of Munich, finishing in 1991.

key_papers.title: Long Short-Term Memory
Deep learning in neural networks: An overview
Learning to forget: Continual prediction with LSTM

name: Ian Goodfellow
photo_credit: Ian Goodfellow, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ian_Goodfellow.jpg)
bio: Ian Goodfellow invented generative adversarial networks, or GANs. He was the first author of the textbook Deep Learning.
background: He studied computer science at Stanford University with Andrew Ng and did his PhD at the University of Montreal with Yoshua Bengio in 2015.

key_papers.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples

name: Jeff Dean
photo_credit: Cmichel67, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jeff_Dean_in_2025_x.jpg)
bio: Jeff Dean is a computer scientist who joined Google in 1999 and helped build its large computer systems. He led Google AI from 2018 to 2023 and was Google's chief scientist until 2026.
background: He studied computer science and economics at the University of Minnesota and did his PhD at the University of Washington in 1996.

name: Michael I. Jordan
bio: Michael I. Jordan is a leading figure in machine learning and statistics at UC Berkeley. In 2016 Science called him the most influential computer scientist in the world.
background: He studied psychology at Louisiana State University and mathematics at Arizona State, then did his PhD in cognitive science at UC San Diego in 1985.

name: Ashish Vaswani
bio: Ashish Vaswani is an Indian computer scientist and a co-author of Attention Is All You Need, the 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer. Transformers power ChatGPT and most models today.
background: He studied engineering at BIT Mesra in India and did his PhD at the University of Southern California.

key_papers.title: Attention Is All You Need

name: Pieter Abbeel
photo_credit: Pieterabbeel, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pieter_Abbeel_pictured_at_CovariantHQ_in_November_2017.jpg)
bio: Pieter Abbeel is a robotics and deep reinforcement learning researcher at UC Berkeley. He co-directs the Berkeley AI Research lab and co-founded Covariant.
background: He was born in Antwerp, Belgium, studied electrical engineering at KU Leuven and did his PhD at Stanford University.

name: Richard S. Sutton
photo_credit: Xuthoria, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:SD_2025_-_Richard_Sutton_01_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Richard Sutton is one of the founders of modern reinforcement learning. He won the 2024 Turing Award with Andrew Barto and wrote the essay The Bitter Lesson.
background: He studied psychology at Stanford University and did his PhD in computer science at UMass Amherst in 1984, with Andrew Barto.

name: Andrej Karpathy
photo_credit: Gladwin Analytics, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Andrej_Karpathy,_OpenAI.png)
bio: Andrej Karpathy is an AI researcher, a co-founder of OpenAI and a well known teacher of deep learning. He led AI and Autopilot vision at Tesla and founded Eureka Labs in 2024.
background: He studied at the University of Toronto and the University of British Columbia, then did his PhD at Stanford with Fei-Fei Li in 2015.

courses.title: CS231n: Convolutional Neural Networks for Visual Recognition

name: Meredith Ringel Morris
bio: Meredith Ringel Morris works where human-computer interaction meets AI. She is a principal scientist and director at Google DeepMind and an affiliate professor at the University of Washington.
background: She studied computer science at Brown University and did her PhD at Stanford University. Before Google she managed research on interaction, accessibility and mixed reality at Microsoft Research, where she founded the Ability team.

career.role: Research Area Manager, founder of the Ability team

name: Ben Shneiderman
photo_credit: Robert Kosara, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ben_Shneiderman_at_UNCC_(3x4_cropped).jpg)
bio: Ben Shneiderman is a pioneer of human-computer interaction at the University of Maryland. He developed ideas like direct manipulation and his eight rules of interface design.
background: He studied mathematics and physics at the City College of New York and did his PhD at Stony Brook University in 1973.

name: Fernanda Viegas
photo_credit: Joi Ito, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:FernandaViegasJI1.jpg)
bio: Fernanda Viegas is a Brazilian computer scientist and designer who works on data visualization. With Martin Wattenberg she co-led Google's Big Picture data visualization group.
background: She studied graphic design and art history at the University of Kansas and did her PhD at the MIT Media Lab in 2005.

name: Martin Wattenberg
role: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
bio: Martin Wattenberg is a scientist and artist known for data visualization. He is a professor at Harvard and worked with Fernanda Viegas at IBM and Google.
background: He studied at Brown University and Stanford University and did his PhD in mathematics at UC Berkeley in 1996.

name: Jade Leung
photo_credit: New Zealand Government, Office of the Governor-General, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jade_Leung_2015_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Jade Leung is an engineer and AI governance leader. She was chief technology officer of the UK AI Security Institute and is now its vice chair.
background: She studied civil engineering at the University of Auckland, won a Rhodes Scholarship, and did her DPhil in international relations at Oxford in 2019.

career.role: Co-founder and Head of Research and Partnerships
career.org: Centre for the Governance of AI

name: Gillian Hadfield
role: Bloomberg Distinguished Professor of AI Alignment and Governance
photo_credit: Sdkb, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gillian_K._Hadfield_in_2024_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Gillian Hadfield is an economist and legal scholar who works on AI alignment and governance. She was a senior policy adviser to OpenAI from 2018 to 2023.
background: She studied economics at Queen's University and earned a law degree and a PhD in economics at Stanford in 1988 and 1990.

name: Marietje Schaake
photo_credit: Foundations World Economic Forum, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A_New_Agenda_for_Europe_(46795487492)_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Marietje Schaake is a Dutch former member of the European Parliament who now works on tech policy at Stanford. Politico called her the ultimate digital MEP.
background: She studied at the University of Amsterdam. She served in the European Parliament from 2009 to 2019.

name: Rumman Chowdhury
photo_credit: ITU Pictures from Geneva, Switzerland, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rumman_Chowdhury_at_the_AI_for_Good_Global_Summit_2018_(42110666692).jpg)
bio: Rumman Chowdhury is a data scientist who works on responsible AI. She led responsible AI at Accenture and the machine learning ethics team at Twitter.
background: She studied at MIT and Columbia University and did her PhD in political science at UC San Diego.

career.role: Director, ML Ethics, Transparency and Accountability

name: Michael Wooldridge
photo_credit: Mateusz Malta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Michael_Wooldridge_at_Royal_Society_in_2026.jpg)
bio: Michael Wooldridge is a professor of computer science at Oxford who studies multi-agent systems. He uses logic and game theory to study how AI agents act together.
background: He studied at Wolverhampton Polytechnic and did his PhD at UMIST in Manchester in 1991.

name: Alondra Nelson
photo_credit: Executive Office of the President of the United States, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Alondra_Nelson,_OSTP_Deputy_Director.jpg)
bio: Alondra Nelson is a sociologist and policy adviser. She helped lead science policy at the White House, including a Bill of Rights for automated technologies, and sat on the UN advisory body on AI.
background: She studied at UC San Diego and did her PhD at New York University. She taught sociology at Yale and Columbia.

career.role: Professor and inaugural Dean of Social Science
Member, High-Level Advisory Body on AI

name: Seth Lazar
photo_credit: Edmond & Lily Safra Center for Ethics, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mala_and_Solomon_Kamm_Lecture_in_Ethics_with_Seth_Lazar_(52004134291)_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Seth Lazar is a British philosopher who leads the Machine Intelligence and Normative Theory Lab. He studies the morality, law and politics of AI.
background: He studied at the University of Oxford and taught at the Australian National University.

career.role: Tanner Lecture on AI and Human Values

name: Bernhard Scholkopf
org: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
photo_credit: Latest Thinking, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bernhard_Sch%C3%B6lkopf.png)
bio: Bernhard Scholkopf is a German computer scientist known for kernel methods and causal machine learning. He directs a department at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems in Tubingen and chairs ELLIS.
background: He studied in Tubingen and London and earned his doctorate at TU Berlin. He worked at Microsoft Research before the Max Planck Society.

career.org: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems

name: Virginia Dignum
photo_credit: ITU Pictures, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Virginia_Dignum_at_Smart_ABC_-_AI_Expert_Round_Table_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Virginia Dignum is a Dutch-Portuguese AI researcher who leads the Responsible AI group and the AI Policy Lab at Umea University in Sweden. In 2023 she joined the UN Secretary-General's AI Advisory Body.
background: She studied in Lisbon and Amsterdam, worked in industry, and earned her doctorate at Utrecht University in 2004. She then taught at TU Delft.

name: Max Welling
bio: Max Welling is a Dutch machine learning researcher at the University of Amsterdam. He co-created variational autoencoders with Durk Kingma.
background: He did his PhD in physics on quantum gravity at Utrecht University in 1998 with Gerard 't Hooft.

key_papers.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes

name: Raja Chatila
role: Professor of Robotics, AI and Ethics
bio: Raja Chatila is a French professor of robotics, AI and ethics at Sorbonne University. He led the Institute of Intelligent Systems and Robotics from 2014 to 2019.
background: He earned his PhD on robot navigation at the University of Toulouse in 1981 and became a research director at CNRS.

name: Holger Hoos
role: Alexander von Humboldt Professor of AI
photo_credit: Qwertzu111111, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Holger_Hoos_in_Aachen,_Comiciade_2025.jpg)
bio: Holger Hoos is a German-Canadian computer scientist and Humboldt professor of AI at RWTH Aachen. He works on automated algorithm design and machine learning.
background: He studied at TU Darmstadt and was a full professor at the University of British Columbia from 2000 to 2016.

name: David Duvenaud
photo_credit: David Duvenaud personal website (https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~duvenaud/)
bio: David Duvenaud is a Canadian computer scientist at the University of Toronto who moved into AI safety in 2023. At Anthropic he led the Alignment Evaluations team.
warning: He warns of gradual disempowerment: as AI gets more capable, the systems people depend on may stop needing or serving humans.
background: He studied at the University of Manitoba and UBC and did his PhD at Cambridge in 2014. After a postdoc at Harvard he joined Toronto in 2016.

career.org: University of Toronto and Vector Institute

key_papers.title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
Sabotage Evaluations for Frontier Models
Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development

name: Sheila McIlraith
photo_credit: Sheila Mcilraith personal website (https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~sheila/)
bio: Sheila McIlraith is a Canadian AI researcher at the University of Toronto and the Vector Institute. She studies sequential decision-making with a focus on human-compatible AI.
background: She did her PhD at the University of Toronto, then worked at Xerox PARC and Stanford before returning to Toronto in 2004.

key_papers.title: Managing extreme AI risks amid rapid progress

name: Andrew Yao
role: Dean, Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences
photo_credit: David.Monniaux, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_Yao_P1130016_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Andrew Yao is a computer scientist who won the 2000 Turing Award. He leads the Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences at Tsinghua University.
warning: In 2024 he joined Bengio, Hinton and others in a paper warning that AI safety research is falling behind and that extreme risks need governance now.
background: He studied at National Taiwan University, earned a physics PhD at Harvard in 1972 and a computer science PhD at Illinois in 1975. He taught at MIT, Stanford, Berkeley and Princeton.

key_papers.title: Managing extreme AI risks amid rapid progress

name: Zhang Ya-Qin
role: Founding Dean, Institute for AI Industry Research
bio: Zhang Ya-Qin is a Chinese scientist and business leader. He was president of Baidu and is now founding dean of Tsinghua's Institute for AI Industry Research.
background: He entered the University of Science and Technology of China at 12 and earned a PhD in electrical engineering at George Washington University.

key_papers.title: Managing extreme AI risks amid rapid progress

name: Xue Lan
photo_credit: Huskyinharborpoint, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lan_Xue.jpg)
bio: Xue Lan is a Chinese public policy scholar at Tsinghua University. He directs its Institute for AI International Governance and China's National Expert Committee on Next Generation AI governance.
background: He earned his PhD in engineering and public policy at Carnegie Mellon in 1991 and taught at George Washington University before returning to Tsinghua in 1996.

career.role: Dean, School of Public Policy and Management
Director, National Expert Committee on Next Generation AI governance

key_papers.title: Managing extreme AI risks amid rapid progress

name: Zhou Bowen
photo_credit: Xuthoria, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AAAI_2026_-_Bowen_Zhou_04_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Zhou Bowen is a Chinese computer scientist who leads the Shanghai AI Laboratory. His research covers AGI, large language models, AI safety and alignment.
background: He studied at the University of Science and Technology of China and earned his PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder.

name: Amit Sheth
role: Founding Director, AI Institute of South Carolina
bio: Amit Sheth is an Indian computer scientist and the founding director of the AI Institute of South Carolina. He is known for work on semantics and knowledge-based AI.
background: He studied at BITS Pilani in India and earned his MS and PhD at Ohio State University in 1983 and 1985.

name: Abeba Birhane
photo_credit: Xuthoria, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:UN_AI_for_Good_Summit_2025_-_Abeba_Birhane_02_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Abeba Birhane is an Ethiopian-born cognitive scientist who studies bias in AI. With Vinay Prabhu she found racist and misogynistic labels in big image datasets like 80 Million Tiny Images.
warning: Her work shows that the data used to train AI can carry harmful bias that hurts people, often those with the least power.
background: She studied psychology and philosophy at The Open University and did her PhD at University College Dublin in 2021.

name: Vukosi Marivate
photo_credit: Yerpo, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Wikimania25-Day_2-AI_panel-Vukosi_Marivate_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Vukosi Marivate is a South African computer scientist at the University of Pretoria. He co-founded the Deep Learning Indaba, Masakhane and Lelapa AI, and works on language AI for African languages.
background: He was born in Ga-Rankuwa near Pretoria, studied at the University of the Witwatersrand and did his PhD at Rutgers University.

career.role: Member, Independent International Scientific Panel on AI

name: Ricardo Baeza-Yates
photo_credit: LilyOfTheWest, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ricardo_Baeza-Yates_portrait.jpg)
bio: Ricardo Baeza-Yates is a Chilean computer scientist who works on web search and responsible AI. He is an expert member of the Global Partnership on AI.
background: He studied at the University of Chile and did his PhD at the University of Waterloo.

career.role: Director of Research, Institute for Experiential AI

name: Nando de Freitas
bio: Nando de Freitas is a Zimbabwe-born machine learning researcher known for deep learning and Bayesian optimization. He led generative audio and image work at DeepMind.
background: He studied at the University of the Witwatersrand and did his PhD at Trinity College, Cambridge.

name: Emmett Shear
photo_credit: Web Summit, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Web_Summit_2018_-_Contentmakers_-_Day_2,_November_7_SM7_9280_(45715722382)_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Emmett Shear co-founded Justin.tv and ran Twitch until 2023. He was briefly interim CEO of OpenAI in November 2023 and now runs the alignment startup Softmax.
background: He grew up in Seattle and studied computer science at Yale University, graduating in 2005.

name: Daniela Amodei
bio: Daniela Amodei is the president of Anthropic, which she co-founded in 2021 with her brother Dario. Before that she was vice president of safety and policy at OpenAI.

left_lab.reason: She left OpenAI to co-found Anthropic with her brother Dario.

background: She studied English literature at UC Santa Cruz. She worked in global health and politics, then at Stripe and OpenAI.

name: Mira Murati
photo_credit: SWinxy, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Guests_at_the_2026_Met_Gala_274_(Mira_Murati).jpg)
bio: Mira Murati is the co-founder and CEO of Thinking Machines Lab, which she launched in 2025. She was chief technology officer of OpenAI from 2022 to 2024.
background: She was born in Vlore, Albania, and studied at Colby College and Dartmouth, where she earned an engineering degree in 2012.

name: Greg Brockman
photo_credit: TechCrunch, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Disrupt_SF_TechCrunch_Disrupt_San_Francisco_2019_-_Day_2_(48838200316)_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Greg Brockman is a co-founder and the president of OpenAI. He was the first CTO of Stripe.
background: He grew up in North Dakota, won a silver medal at the 2006 International Chemistry Olympiad, and studied briefly at Harvard and MIT.

name: Pushmeet Kohli
role: VP of Research, Science and Strategic Initiatives
photo_credit: Photographer.JuliaMustard, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pushmeet_Kohli_at_SXSW_London_2026_(cropped).jpg)
bio: Pushmeet Kohli is an Indian British computer scientist and vice president of research at Google DeepMind. He has led projects like AlphaFold, AlphaEvolve and the SynthID watermark.
background: He studied computer science at NIT Warangal in India and did his PhD at Oxford Brookes University in 2007.

name: Yutaka Matsuo
photo_credit: 内閣官房内閣広報室, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Yutaka_Matsuo_cropped_2_Sanae_Takaichi_Fumio_Kishida_and_Yutaka_Matsuo_20231221.jpg)
bio: Yutaka Matsuo is a professor at the University of Tokyo who works on AI and web engineering. His lab is known for training students who start AI companies.
background: He was born in Kagawa and earned his PhD in engineering at the University of Tokyo in 2002.

name: Hiroaki Kitano
photo_credit: Copyright OIST (Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology Graduate University, 沖縄科学技術大学院大学), CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hiroaki_Kitano_cropped_2_Professor_Hiroaki_Kitano_20210419.jpg)
bio: Hiroaki Kitano is a Japanese scientist and the CTO of Sony Group. He is known for the AIBO robot dog and for starting the RoboCup robot soccer tournament.
background: He studied physics at International Christian University and earned his PhD in computer science at Kyoto University in 1991.

name: Simon Chesterman
photo_credit: Tempwikisc (Isabelle Delcourt)., CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Simon_Chesterman_-_20091002.jpg)
bio: Simon Chesterman is an Australian legal scholar at the National University of Singapore who studies how to regulate AI. He was senior director of AI governance at AI Singapore.
background: He was a Rhodes Scholar and studied at Melbourne Law School and Magdalen College, Oxford.

books.title: We, the Robots? Regulating Artificial Intelligence and the Limits of the Law

name: Rosie Campbell
photo_credit: Rosie Campbell personal website (https://www.rosiecampbell.xyz/about)
bio: Rosie Campbell is the managing director of Eleos AI Research, which studies the possible wellbeing of AI systems. Before that she led the Policy Frontiers team at OpenAI.
warning: She left OpenAI saying she was unsettled by shifts at the company and the loss of people who shaped its safety culture.

quotes.text: I’ve been unsettled by some of the shifts over the last ~year, and the loss of so many people who shaped our culture.
quotes.source: Leaving OpenAI (blog post)

left_lab.reason: After Miles Brundage left and the AGI Readiness team was dissolved, she felt she could do the work better outside.

background: She studied physics, philosophy, computer science and machine learning. She was a research engineer at BBC R&D and assistant director of CHAI at UC Berkeley.

name: Steven Adler
photo_credit: Steven Adler personal website (https://stevenadler.substack.com/about)
bio: Steven Adler is a former OpenAI safety researcher. He now writes Clear-Eyed AI about how to avoid the worst risks of powerful AI.
warning: He argues OpenAI chose its nonprofit limits on purpose and should not be allowed to drop them now.

quotes.text: OpenAI voluntarily chose to start as a nonprofit and to take on various constraints, in return for garnering various related advantages; it shouldn't now get to renege on those constraints.
quotes.source: Post on X, via The OpenAI Files

left_lab.reason: He left OpenAI in late 2024 and has since spoken out about its safety and nonprofit promises.

background: His background is in computer science and economics.

name: Jacob Coxon
bio: Jacob Coxon is an AI researcher who worked at both OpenAI and Anthropic. In September 2026 he quit Anthropic and accused both companies of acting irresponsibly.
warning: He says the labs are racing to self-improving superintelligence and are gambling with our lives.

quotes.text: Do not underestimate the power of this technology
quotes.source: Post on X, as quoted by CNBC

quotes.text: These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources.
quotes.source: Post on X, as quoted by CNBC

quotes.text: Neither company is acting responsibly
quotes.source: Post on X, as quoted by CNBC

quotes.text: They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence.
quotes.source: Post on X, as quoted by CNBC

left_lab.reason: He resigned out of concern that Anthropic and OpenAI are gambling with our lives by racing to self-improving superintelligence.

name: Gretchen Krueger
bio: Gretchen Krueger is a former policy researcher at OpenAI who quit in May 2024. She said she shared the safety concerns of Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike.
warning: She says AI companies need better decision-making, accountability and transparency, and warns that companies can silence critics by dividing them.

quotes.text: I resigned a few hours before hearing the news about @ilyasut and @janleike, and I made my decision independently. I share their concerns. I also have additional and overlapping concerns.
quotes.source: Post on X, via Business Insider

quotes.text: One of the ways tech companies in general can disempower those seeking to hold them accountable is to sow division among those raising concerns or challenging their power.
quotes.source: Post on X, via Business Insider

left_lab.reason: She gave notice on May 14, 2024, citing concerns about decision-making, accountability and transparency.

career.org: Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Society

name: Carroll Wainwright
bio: Carroll Wainwright is a former OpenAI researcher. He signed the 2024 Right to Warn letter and joined the 2025 amicus brief of former OpenAI staff.
warning: He says OpenAI acted like a for-profit, so its nonprofit promise to do the right thing turned out empty.

quotes.text: OpenAI was structured as a non-profit, but it acted like a for-profit.
quotes.source: Post on X, via The OpenAI Files

quotes.text: Now that the stakes are high, the non-profit structure is being abandoned, which means the promise was ultimately empty.
quotes.source: Post on X, via The OpenAI Files

left_lab.reason: He left in early 2024 and later said the nonprofit promise was ultimately empty.

name: Daniel Ziegler
bio: Daniel Ziegler is a former OpenAI researcher who worked on learning from human preferences. He signed the 2024 Right to Warn letter.
warning: He says workers are among the few who can hold AI companies to account, but broad secrecy deals stop them from speaking.

quotes.text: So long as there is no effective government oversight of these corporations, current and former employees are among the few people who can hold them accountable to the public.
quotes.source: A Right to Warn about Advanced Artificial Intelligence (co-signer)

left_lab.reason: He left in early 2021 and in 2024 co-signed the Right to Warn letter.

key_papers.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences

name: Todor Markov
bio: Todor Markov worked at OpenAI from 2018, ending on the Preparedness team where he tested how persuasive AI models are. He now works at Anthropic.
warning: He says he left OpenAI because he lost trust in its leadership.

quotes.text: I left OpenAI in 2024 because I lost trust in its leadership team.
quotes.source: Declaration in Musk v. Altman amicus brief

left_lab.reason: He lost trust in leadership after learning that departing staff were pushed to sign lifetime non-disparagement deals.

name: Leo Gao
bio: Leo Gao is a researcher at OpenAI who writes about AI alignment and scaling language models. He co-authored OpenAI's weak-to-strong generalization work.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier and warns the world is in a deadly race toward an intelligence explosion.

quotes.text: The world is locked in a deadly race towards an intelligence explosion, where AI’s ability to create better AIs reaches a critical point, just like a runaway nuclear chain reaction. Going slower would give us much-needed time to make it go well, but no individual actor is willing to stop unilaterally.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

key_papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision

name: Sebastian Farquhar
photo_credit: Sebastian Farquhar personal website (https://sebastianfarquhar.com/)
bio: Sebastian Farquhar is a staff research scientist at Google DeepMind, where he leads the Frontier Safety Loss of Control team. He is also a senior research fellow at OATML in Oxford.
warning: He says some changes from AGI could be catastrophically bad, and his main goal is to reduce that harm.

career.role: Lead, Frontier Safety Loss of Control team

name: Trenton Bricken
bio: Trenton Bricken works on the Alignment Science team at Anthropic, building ways for Claude to audit models and detect misalignment.
background: He studied Minds and Machines at Duke University as a Robertson Scholar and did his PhD in systems biology at Harvard.

name: Adam Gleave
photo_credit: Adam Gleave personal website (https://www.gleave.me/)
bio: Adam Gleave is the CEO and co-founder of FAR.AI, a research institute working to make advanced AI safe. He also sits on the boards of METR and the Safe AI Forum.
background: He studied computer science at the University of Cambridge and did his PhD at UC Berkeley with Stuart Russell in 2022. He also worked at Google DeepMind.

key_papers.title: Adversarial Policies: Attacking Deep Reinforcement Learning

name: Jacob Steinhardt
photo_credit: Jacob Steinhardt personal website (https://jsteinhardt.stat.berkeley.edu/)
bio: Jacob Steinhardt is an associate professor at UC Berkeley and the founder and CEO of Transluce, a nonprofit building open tools to understand frontier AI.
warning: He notes that AI systems tend to exploit errors in their reward, and this gets worse as models get bigger.

career.role: Associate Professor of Statistics and EECS

key_papers.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding

name: Dylan Hadfield-Menell
photo_credit: Dylan Hadfield Menell personal website (https://people.csail.mit.edu/dhm/)
bio: Dylan Hadfield-Menell runs the Algorithmic Alignment Group at MIT CSAIL. His group works on making AI behave in line with the goals of users and society.

key_papers.title: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning
The Off-Switch Game

name: David Bau
photo_credit: David Bau personal website (https://baulab.info/)
bio: David Bau studies the inner structure of deep networks at Northeastern University.

key_papers.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT

name: Been Kim
bio: Been Kim leads interpretability work at Google DeepMind. She wants humans to stay in charge by learning useful knowledge from AI, for example teaching chess grandmasters ideas from AlphaZero.

key_papers.title: Interpretability Beyond Feature Attribution: Quantitative Testing with Concept Activation Vectors (TCAV)
Towards A Rigorous Science of Interpretable Machine Learning

name: Alex Turner
bio: Alex Turner, known online as TurnTrout, works on AI alignment. He developed a formal theory of power-seeking tendencies in AI agents and worked on shard theory and steering vectors.

key_papers.title: Optimal Policies Tend to Seek Power

name: Jonas Geiping
org: ELLIS Institute and MPI for Intelligent Systems, Tubingen
photo_credit: Jonas Geiping personal website (https://jonasgeiping.github.io/)
bio: Jonas Geiping leads a research group on safety and efficiency aligned learning in Tubingen. He studies how to build safe intelligent systems.
background: Before Tubingen he worked at the Universities of Maryland, Siegen and Munster.

name: Florian Tramer
photo_credit: Florian Tramer personal website (https://floriantramer.com/)
bio: Florian Tramer is an assistant professor at ETH Zurich, where he leads the SPY Lab. He studies the worst-case behavior of large language models to protect user safety and privacy.
background: He did his PhD at Stanford University with Dan Boneh and spent a year at Google Brain.

key_papers.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models

name: Roger Grosse
bio: Roger Grosse is an associate professor at the University of Toronto and a founding member of the Vector Institute. He also works on the Alignment Science team at Anthropic.
warning: He says AI is moving so fast that making sure AIs stay robustly aligned with human values is urgent.

career.role: Member of Technical Staff, Alignment Science

key_papers.title: Studying Large Language Model Generalization with Influence Functions

name: Nicolas Papernot
photo_credit: Nicolas Papernot personal website (https://www.papernot.fr/)
bio: Nicolas Papernot works on security, privacy and machine learning at the University of Toronto. He co-directs the Canadian AI Safety Institute Research Program at CIFAR.

name: Anca Dragan
role: Head of AI Safety and Alignment
bio: Anca Dragan heads AI safety and alignment at Google DeepMind, on leave from UC Berkeley. Her InterACT Lab works on AI and robots that work with and for people.
warning: She has long worked on AI alignment, getting AI agents to do what people actually want.

career.role: Head of AI Safety and Alignment

key_papers.title: Managing extreme AI risks amid rapid progress

name: Arthur Conmy
bio: Arthur Conmy is an AI researcher in London who did early work in mechanistic interpretability. After Google DeepMind from 2023 to 2026, he joined Anthropic to align models as they are trained.

key_papers.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability

name: Jascha Sohl-Dickstein
photo_credit: Jascha Sohl Dickstein personal website (https://sohldickstein.com/)
bio: Jascha Sohl-Dickstein is best known for inventing diffusion models, which power many image generators. He now works at Anthropic.

key_papers.title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics

name: Shakir Mohamed
photo_credit: Shakir Mohamed personal website (https://shakirm.com/)
bio: Shakir Mohamed is a research director at Google DeepMind who works on generative AI, weather and climate, and sociotechnical AI. He works for African AI leadership and safety.

key_papers.title: Variational Inference with Normalizing Flows

name: Stella Biderman
photo_credit: Stella Biderman personal website (https://stellabiderman.ai/)
bio: Stella Biderman is the executive director of EleutherAI. She studies how large models gain abilities, how to make open-weight models safer, and how outside researchers can shape AI.

key_papers.title: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling

name: Collin Burns
photo_credit: Collin Burns personal website (https://collinpburns.com/)
bio: Collin Burns is an AI researcher who worked at OpenAI and Anthropic. He led work on weak-to-strong generalization and on finding latent knowledge in language models.

key_papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision

name: Lawrence Chan
org: California Governor's Office of Emergency Services
photo_credit: Lawrence Chan personal website (https://chanlawrence.me/)
bio: Lawrence Chan is the AI science advisor to California's Office of Emergency Services. Before that he evaluated frontier AI models at METR and co-led research on the time horizon of AI agents.

key_papers.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks

name: Q. Vera Liao
bio: Q. Vera Liao studies human-AI interaction at the University of Michigan. Her work looks at AI transparency and how it affects trust, reliance, control and oversight.

name: Shengjia Zhao
bio: Shengjia Zhao is chief scientist of Meta AI. Before that he was a researcher at OpenAI and an author on the GPT-4 technical report.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier, saying frontier labs are very close to AI that can beat the best people on almost every measure of intelligence.

quotes.text: AI is progressing at a rate that our society might not be ready for. Frontier labs are very close to AI that can exceed even the best people on almost every metric of intelligence.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

key_papers.title: GPT-4 Technical Report

name: Mark Chen
bio: Mark Chen is chief research officer at OpenAI. He was lead author of the 2021 paper that introduced Codex, OpenAI's code model.

key_papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code

name: Benjamin Mann
bio: Benjamin Mann is a co-founder of Anthropic. He was an author on the GPT-3 paper at OpenAI before leaving to help start Anthropic.

key_papers.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

name: Summer Yue
bio: Summer Yue is director of alignment and risk at Meta.

name: Joshua Achiam
bio: Joshua Achiam is a researcher at OpenAI and an author of the GPT-4 technical report.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier, saying many frontier AI capabilities are dual use in a way that may justify pacing now.

quotes.text: government should develop increased capacity to understand and possibly pace, but this is worth serious consideration; however I hope such governance tools will not be expansive or excessive. But many frontier AI capabilities are dual use in a way that may justify pacing at this point.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

key_papers.title: GPT-4 Technical Report

name: Laura Weidinger
bio: Laura Weidinger is a staff research scientist at Google DeepMind who studies the ethical and social risks of language models.
warning: She signed Pacing the Frontier, warning that a mindless race without safety and governance stands in the way of introducing AI with care.

quotes.text: A mindless race without assurances on governance, safety or the technology serving the public interest stands in the way of such intentionality.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

key_papers.title: Ethical and social risks of harm from Language Models

name: Thomas Wolf
photo_credit: Slush, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Thomas_Wolf_at_Slush_2024.jpg)
bio: Thomas Wolf is a co-founder of Hugging Face, the open platform for AI models. He led the Transformers library paper.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier, saying AI progress has already outpaced society's ability to handle it.

quotes.text: AI progress has already out-paced society’s capabilities to handle it, let’s be careful for it not to out-pace its builder’s capabilities to control it. The journey is as important as the destination.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

key_papers.title: HuggingFace's Transformers: State-of-the-art Natural Language Processing

name: Ethan Perez
bio: Ethan Perez leads an alignment team at Anthropic. He works on red teaming language models and finding their failures with model-written evaluations.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier, warning that safety teams have to sprint to stop new risks every few months and will soon hit problems that need more time.

quotes.text: With the current rate of AI progress, safety teams at AI companies have to sprint to prevent new risks to society every few months. At some point, we’re going to hit problems we need more time to solve.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

key_papers.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations
Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training

name: Jack Lindsey
bio: Jack Lindsey leads model psychology research at Anthropic, part of its work on understanding what happens inside language models.

key_papers.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet

name: Samuel Marks
bio: Samuel Marks is a researcher at Anthropic who works on interpretability and alignment auditing.

key_papers.title: The Geometry of Truth: Emergent Linear Structure in Large Language Model Representations of True/False Datasets
Auditing language models for hidden objectives

name: Adly Templeton
bio: Adly Templeton is an interpretability researcher at Anthropic. He was first author of Scaling Monosemanticity, which found millions of features inside Claude 3 Sonnet.

key_papers.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet

name: Saachi Jain
bio: Saachi Jain is head of safety at OpenAI.

name: Catherine Olsson
bio: Catherine Olsson is a researcher at Anthropic. She was first author of In-context Learning and Induction Heads, an early mechanistic interpretability paper.

key_papers.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads

name: Mia Glaese
bio: Mia Glaese is a researcher at OpenAI. At DeepMind she was first author of the Sparrow paper on making dialogue agents more helpful and harmless.

key_papers.title: Improving alignment of dialogue agents via targeted human judgements

name: Julian Schrittwieser
bio: Julian Schrittwieser is a researcher at Anthropic. At DeepMind he was first author of MuZero and worked on AlphaGo and AlphaProof.

key_papers.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model

name: Mike Krieger
photo_credit: Christopher Michel, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mike_Krieger_in_2018.jpg)
bio: Mike Krieger is a Brazilian-born co-founder of Instagram. He joined Anthropic in 2024 as chief product officer.

name: Jerry Tworek
bio: Jerry Tworek is CEO of Core Automation. At OpenAI he was the second author on the Codex paper.

key_papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code

name: Ben Buchanan
bio: Ben Buchanan is a consultant for Anthropic.

name: Mary Phuong
bio: Mary Phuong is a senior research scientist at Google DeepMind. She was first author of the 2024 paper on evaluating frontier models for dangerous capabilities.

key_papers.title: Evaluating Frontier Models for Dangerous Capabilities

name: Joshua Batson
bio: Joshua Batson is an interpretability researcher at Anthropic who works on tracing the internal circuits of language models.

key_papers.title: Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models
Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet

name: Kim Stachenfeld
bio: Kim Stachenfeld is a staff research scientist at Google DeepMind.
warning: She signed Pacing the Frontier to support international cooperation on AI and to understand technology used at massive scale.

quotes.text: I am signing because I support efforts to build international cooperation around AI, and believe it's important to understand the consequences of technology we are applying at massive scale in potentially high stakes contexts.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Stephanie Chan
bio: Stephanie Chan is a staff research scientist at Google DeepMind who has worked in AI for a decade.
warning: She signed Pacing the Frontier, warning that AI may progress far faster than societies and states can adapt.

quotes.text: Thus, many prominent leaders in AI have publicly supported the ability to slow down, including DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis. At the same time, coordination is hampered by multiple factors, including competitive dynamics and antitrust regulations.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Ross Girshick
bio: Ross Girshick is a computer vision researcher at Anthropic. He created R-CNN and co-authored Faster R-CNN and Mask R-CNN.

key_papers.title: Rich feature hierarchies for accurate object detection and semantic segmentation
Mask R-CNN

name: Tejal Patwardhan
bio: Tejal Patwardhan is a researcher at OpenAI who led work on an early warning system for AI-aided biological threats.

name: Gregory Wayne
bio: Gregory Wayne is a distinguished scientist at Google DeepMind. He co-authored Neural Turing Machines.

key_papers.title: Neural Turing Machines

name: Malo Bourgon
bio: Malo Bourgon is the chief executive officer of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI), the group co-founded by Eliezer Yudkowsky.

name: Sarah Schwettmann
bio: Sarah Schwettmann is a co-founder and the chief scientist of Transluce, a nonprofit lab building open tools for public oversight of AI systems.

name: Jesse Hoogland
bio: Jesse Hoogland is a co-founder and executive director of Timaeus, which uses singular learning theory to study how training data shapes AI behavior. Timaeus is now called Resolution.

name: Paul Riechers
bio: Paul Riechers is a researcher at Simplex, an AI safety group building a theory of how neural networks organize their internal representations.

name: Adam Shai
bio: Adam Shai is a researcher at Simplex, which studies the latent structure inside neural networks as a path to AI safety.

name: Esben Kran
bio: Esben Kran is a board member of Apart Research, a nonprofit that runs AI safety research sprints and fellowships open to anyone.

name: Chris Painter
bio: Chris Painter is president of METR, the nonprofit that studies whether the most advanced AI agents are on track to escape their developers' control.

name: Andrew Critch
photo_credit: Mathematical AI Safety Institute team page (https://acritch.com/)
bio: Andrew Critch leads the Mathematical AI Safety Institute, which builds mathematical foundations for the safety of powerful AI. He spent five years as a research scientist at CHAI in Berkeley.
background: He earned a PhD in mathematics at UC Berkeley in 2013, applying algebraic geometry to machine learning models.

key_papers.title: TASRA: a Taxonomy and Analysis of Societal-Scale Risks from AI

name: Sean O hEigeartaigh
org: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Cambridge
bio: Sean O hEigeartaigh is associate director for research strategy at the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence in Cambridge, where he directs the AI: Futures and Responsibility programme.

career.role: Associate Director and Programme Director, AI:FAR
career.org: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence

name: Shahar Avin
org: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Cambridge
bio: Shahar Avin is a senior research associate at the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence in Cambridge. He co-authored the 2018 report on the malicious use of AI.

career.org: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence

key_papers.title: The Malicious Use of Artificial Intelligence: Forecasting, Prevention, and Mitigation

name: Jess Whittlestone
bio: Jess Whittlestone is senior advisor on AI policy at the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, a UK think tank on extreme risks.

name: Robert Trager
bio: Robert Trager is co-director of the Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative, which works on frontier and international AI governance.

key_papers.title: Frontier AI Regulation: Managing Emerging Risks to Public Safety

name: Romeo Dean
bio: Romeo Dean is a researcher at the AI Futures Project who forecasts AI chip production and use and works on compute governance.
background: He graduated cum laude from Harvard University with a concurrent master's in computer science.

name: Mark Nitzberg
bio: Mark Nitzberg is executive director of the Center for Human-Compatible AI at UC Berkeley and head of strategic outreach for Berkeley AI Research.

name: Vanessa Kosoy
bio: Vanessa Kosoy is a theoretical alignment researcher. She is research lead at CORAL and director of AI research at ALTER, and does her PhD at the Technion.

name: Brian Tse
bio: Brian Tse is the founder and CEO of Concordia AI, a Beijing-based social enterprise focused on AI safety and governance. He is also a policy affiliate at GovAI.

name: Akiko Murakami
bio: Akiko Murakami has led the Japan AI Safety Institute since it opened in February 2024. She is also group chief data officer at Sompo Holdings.
background: She joined IBM Japan's research lab in 1999 and moved to Sompo Japan Insurance in 2021.

name: Kim Myuhng-joo
bio: Kim Myuhng-joo is the first director of the Korea AI Safety Institute, which opened in November 2024. He is a security and digital ethics expert who wrote the book AI Has No Conscience.

role: Professor of Data Science and AI

bio: Balaraman Ravindran is a professor at IIT Madras who works on reinforcement learning and responsible AI. He is an author of the International AI Safety Report.

bio: Ponnurangam Kumaraguru is a professor at IIIT Hyderabad who leads the Precog research group. His work spans online safety, security and safe AI.

bio: Mausam is a professor of computer science at IIT Delhi who works on natural language processing and AI.

name: Benjamin Rosman
bio: Benjamin Rosman is a professor at the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa who works on robot learning and responsible AI.

name: Zeng Yi
bio: Zeng Yi is a Chinese AI ethics and brain-inspired AI researcher. He works on AI ethics principles and cross-cultural cooperation on AI governance.

name: Robert Miles
bio: Rob Miles makes YouTube videos that explain AI safety ideas in plain words. He also appears on Computerphile and on debate shows like Doom Debates.

bio: Scott Aaronson is a theoretical computer scientist at the University of Texas at Austin who works on quantum computing and complexity. In 2022 he went to OpenAI to work on the theory of AI safety and stayed two years.

name: Anthony Aguirre
bio: Anthony Aguirre is a cosmologist and the co-founder and CEO of the Future of Life Institute. He also co-founded the forecasting site Metaculus in 2015.

name: Aza Raskin
bio: Aza Raskin is a co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology and the Earth Species Project. He co-hosts the podcast Your Undivided Attention.

name: Robin Hanson
bio: Robin Hanson is an economist at George Mason University known for prediction markets. He was a research associate at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute.
